quest.title: Mask
quest.description: Lynette decides to return to the reception...

talks.objective: Go to the second floor to pass the time
Go back to the first floor to take the envelope
Activate search mode and investigate the documents

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Original Script
dialogues.text: (After a quick read through the script, I understand the gist of the story.)

talks.objective: Activate search mode and investigate the documents

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Manuscript
dialogues.text: (The reason it's so hard to read is that it's been edited with correction fluid multiple times. I'd estimate that each line was rewritten at least three times... Looks like Merieux wasn't happy with his edits.)

talks.objective: Activate search mode and investigate the documents

dialogues.speaker: Investigation Notes
dialogues.text: (Skimming through the early newspaper clippings, none of the headlines mention Director Merieux...)

dialogues.speaker: Investigation Notes
dialogues.text: (In more recent years, there are many reports praising Merieux as a forward-thinking director, one of the greats of his era...)

talks.objective: Activate search mode and investigate the documents

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Old Drafts
dialogues.text: (The photos from recent years show fancy venues and polished sets, but the earlier photos show much humbler venues.)

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Old Drafts
dialogues.text: (The cast list shows that in recent years, Merieux has collaborated with many famous celebrities, but their acting chops are disputed... And Maloney is listed as an investor.)

talks.objective: Activate search mode and investigate the documents

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Official Script
dialogues.text: (After a quick read through the script, I understand the gist of the story.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I was too busy enjoying Hotel Debord's desserts to pay attention to what was going on downstairs...)

talks.objective: Continue with the second half of the performance

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Think back to what was happening on the first floor while we were taking some time out...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Examine the letter to see if there is anything amiss...)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'm an outsider to this show, so it's not my place to compare the final production to earlier drafts of the script. I'll be careful to put any initial impression I had after reading it to one side when I'm reviewing the show on the record.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hmm... Yes, the only people qualified to compare the stage show and the script are the cast and crew. Or maybe Merieux alone.

dialogues.speaker: Jaiques & Cyril
dialogues.text: Me neither!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: [Performance] What's she talking about? Never heard of it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wait and see how things play out.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tea party mode...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There's nothing else of note...)

dialogues.speaker: Investigation Notes
dialogues.text: (There are newspaper clippings in amongst the notes. They're about shows of different styles. Those on the first few pages have turned yellow, which means they must be quite old.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: [Investigation] (Look for mentions of Merieux.)

dialogues.speaker: Investigation Notes
dialogues.text: (Merieux's name does appear in some earlier clippings, but mostly in articles bemoaning "A Series of Lukewarm Receptions for an Experimental Art Form" and "Empty Seats at Avant-Garde Play Despite Critical Acclaim"...)

dialogues.speaker: Investigation Notes
dialogues.text: (In more recent years, there are many reports praising Merieux as a forward-thinking director, one of the greats of his era...)

dialogues.speaker: Investigation Notes
dialogues.text: (The articles are written by a variety of authors from an eclectic range of fields. Corentin and Amaury are the most prolific authors.)

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Old Drafts
dialogues.text: (These scripts seem to be Merieux's older works. Some photographs of the live performances are attached.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: [Investigation] (Skim through...)

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Old Drafts
dialogues.text: (The photos from recent years show fancy venues and polished sets, but the earlier photos show much humbler venues.)

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Old Drafts
dialogues.text: (I don't see anything else noteworthy.)

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Official Script
dialogues.text: (The official script for The Lost Puppet details how the dancing puppet protagonist is rejected by humanity and then begins searching for the meaning of life...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: [Investigation] (Read carefully...)

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Official Script
dialogues.text: (In Act IV, the protagonist loses the ability to dance due to wear-and-tear in her circuitry. There's a note saying: "Some cursory movements to get the point across will suffice. The audience's focus will be on the fancy set and the extras.")

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Original Script
dialogues.text: (Let's see what differences there are between the current version of The Lost Puppet and the original script.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: [Investigation] (Read carefully...)

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Original Script
dialogues.text: (Act IV seems to be a solo performance by the protagonist, and the set is just some decrepit ruins. There's a note saying: "This will focus the audience's attention on the solo performer.")

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Manuscript
dialogues.text: (Merieux's original script is littered with amendments. It's practically illegible.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: [Investigation] (Read carefully...)

dialogues.speaker: Investigate Manuscript
dialogues.text: (...Nope, I can't read this at all.)

dialogues.speaker: Jaiques
dialogues.text: ...Do you think this move needs jazzing up a little?

dialogues.speaker: Cyril
dialogues.text: Not jazzing up, per se. I was thinking more, like... break it down, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Gillian
dialogues.text: Ginna? ...You snuck in? When? ...I thought I told you, no visiting me at work...

dialogues.speaker: Ginna
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Gillian... But I had to come...

dialogues.speaker: Jaiques
dialogues.text: I wonder what got into Director Merieux...

dialogues.speaker: Gillian
dialogues.text: Maybe he's been quietly struggling with something...

dialogues.speaker: Gillian
dialogues.text: ...That's strange. I could have sworn I heard a voice just now...

dialogues.speaker: Observe Crowd
dialogues.text: (People are excitedly discussing Lynette's debut performance...)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Crowd
dialogues.text: (People are analyzing Merieux's techniques from a classical perspective...)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Crowd
dialogues.text: (Everyone is debating the performance of each actor...)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Crowd
dialogues.text: (These people seem to be discussing the content of tomorrow's newspapers. Best not get too close...)
